source_name: OpenWay Group — Way4 platform customer case studies and blog
why_relevant: Way4 is one of the two dominant switch/card-management platforms in the region; OpenWay publishes named bank case studies with migration detail. Useful to establish whether a Kosovo issuer/acquirer runs Way4 versus SmartVista or TranzWare, i.e. which vendor's announcements to watch.

source_name: Software Group — payment switch and card management solution / client references
why_relevant: Bulgarian-origin regional fintech integrator selling switch/CMS and agent-banking platforms into SEE microfinance and mid-tier banks — a plausible supplier tier for Kosovo's smaller banks and MFIs; its client pages name institutions.

source_name: Euronet Worldwide — investor newsroom (Independent ATM Deployment market entries)
why_relevant: Euronet announces every new IAD country entry and ATM/deposit-terminal network launch with counts. Kosovo was not found among announced markets in this pass, so this source functions as an early-warning tripwire for a non-bank ATM operator entering Kosovo — a structural change to ATM statistics.

source_name: ATM Marketplace — vendor company media pages and deployment news
why_relevant: Trade aggregator that indexes OEM/vendor press releases by company (Diebold Nixdorf, Wincor Nixdorf, Euronet, NCR), so it captures vendor deployment claims even when the vendor site is bot-defended or the release is delisted. Good single watchpoint for many vendors at once.

source_name: Electronic Payments International — Kosovo region archive
why_relevant: A dedicated Kosovo tag page on a payments trade title — a pre-filtered feed of vendor and processor announcements touching Kosovo (it already carries the Quipu/Compass Plus contactless story). Very low-cost standing monitor for this cell.

source_name: CACTTUS sh.a. — Kosovo ICT system integrator (banking sector clients)
why_relevant: Largest Kosovo-headquartered ICT integrator (est. 2003, Kosovo + Albania), doing system integration, infrastructure and security for regulated industries. Its client/reference and news pages are a local-language pointer to which Kosovo banks buy which infrastructure, and to partner OEMs behind terminal estates.

source_name: STIKK — Kosovo ICT Association member directory
why_relevant: Sector association directory enumerating Kosovo ICT companies with self-declared specialisations — the cheapest way to enumerate the local integrator/reseller layer that installs and services ATM/POS estates for Kosovo banks, and to build the actor map for this cell in Albanian.

source_name: KIESA / Kosovo Exporters Directory (Ministry of Industry, Entrepreneurship and Trade)
why_relevant: Official directory listing Kosovo companies by sector, including ICT firms serving banking. Government-maintained, so it is a durable and citable actor-map source for the local vendor/integrator layer in Albanian.

source_name: ATK Kosovo — register of authorised fiscal-device suppliers
why_relevant: The Tax Administration publishes the list of certified fiscal-device (fiscal cash register / fiscal POS) suppliers. In Kosovo the fiscal-device vendor layer overlaps with the merchant POS-integration layer, so this official register is a rare authoritative, exhaustive vendor list adjacent to card-accepting terminal deployment.

source_name: Kosovo commercial bank product pages as vendor tell-tales (Raiffeisen Kosovo RaiPOS, BPB contactless ATMs, ProCredit 24/7 Zones, TEB, BKT Kosova)
why_relevant: Bank product and network pages disclose the technology generation actually deployed (SoftPOS/tap-to-phone, contactless cardless ATM withdrawal, deposit-capable ATMs, 24/7 self-service zones) and often the branded vendor product name — letting vendor claims be triangulated and dated against the operator's own site.

source_name: Entrust / Evolis / IDEMIA — card issuance and instant-issuance vendor sites
why_relevant: Card-personalisation hardware and service suppliers whose partner-locator and case-study pages identify the personalisation bureau serving a market. Relevant to Kosovo given a personalisation centre operates locally (Quipu); these vendors' partner listings can name the Kosovo reseller.

Kosovo-focused Albanian-language economy news site that publishes near-monthly write-ups of BQK commercial-bank statistics (deposits, gross loans, assets, interest rates) with precise dates and euro figures, often ahead of/instead of English coverage. Directly restates payment- and banking-market numbers useful for A4 market statistics.

One of Kosovo's highest-traffic Albanian news portals with a dedicated economy section; covers payment-system regulation (e.g. the 2,000 EUR cash-payment cap effective 1 June 2026), e-Kosova payment rollout, and BQK/ATK statements. Good for precise event dating on cash-usage and digital-payment policy.

Kosovo's paper of record online; economy and 'Arbëri' desks carry policy-grade reporting on financial sector, AML/cash usage (e.g. GI-TOC money-laundering coverage) and BQK announcements. Higher editorial standard than the mass portals, useful for corroboration.

National news agency; publishes analytical pieces quoting ex-officials and economists on payment-system rules and cash limits, and routinely relays BQK/ATK press material with dates. Agency copy is widely syndicated, so it is a good single capture point.

Investigative outlet focused on corruption, fraud and abuse; covers bank-related court cases, card fraud, procurement and financial-sector oversight — the kind of detail that never appears in BQK aggregates. Also carries sponsored/industry announcements (e.g. BKT Kosova–KESCO e-payment agreement) that flag payment-market changes.

High-traffic Albanian portal that turns BQK credit/deposit aggregates into dated news stories (e.g. household indebtedness / total bank loan value). Useful as a redundancy channel and for headline framing of banking-market trends.

Kosovo's dedicated business/economy news brand; the natural home for bank-network, card-payment and BQK-statistics reporting in Albanian. Referenced in search results as a source for Kosovo banking-sector economic news, though no article URL was captured in this pass.

Aggregates the Albanian-language economy feeds of most Kosovo outlets in one place with country filter (c=K). Best single discovery surface for finding which portals are reporting a given BQK figure and for snowballing to outlets not yet on the list.

Example of the dense layer of Kosovo municipal/local Albanian portals that republish national banking-statistics stories; useful mainly as a mirror when a national outlet's page is down or altered, and as evidence of how widely a figure circulated.

Major Kosovo TV broadcaster whose economy desk interviews BQK officials, bankers and ATK on air; TV interviews frequently produce figures (branch counts, ATM/POS numbers, payment volumes) that are never published in written institutional form.

Albanian-language outlet with a Kosovo desk publishing macro-economic analysis pieces (e.g. on early elections and economic uncertainty) that contextualise banking and payment-market data. Useful for narrative and expert quotes rather than raw figures.

Albania's leading business/finance magazine; covers Kosovo payment-policy changes (e.g. the 2,000 EUR cash ban) with a financial-sector lens and often adds comparative Albania/Kosovo figures. Cross-border Albanian-language coverage that Kosovo-only crawls would miss.
Tirana-based daily that covers Kosovo payment regulation and ATK enforcement; useful as a corroboration mirror and for capturing the wording of official warnings on cash-payment limits.
Albanian-language portal republishing Kosovo payment-regulation news with dated URLs; low editorial value but a reliable date-stamped mirror for the cash-limit story cluster.
Regional desk of an Albanian outlet carrying Kosovo payment/cash-regulation items; another mirror in the Albanian-language republication network, helpful for establishing publication timing spread.

Albanian-language portal reporting on tightening cash-payment limits and the financial sector's pushback; relevant to A4 cash-usage tracking and shows industry-association reactions that rarely appear in central-bank material.
